wa_icicle_buttress.blurb: A large, tiered roadside buttress in Icicle Canyon, a few miles up the road from Leavenworth. Most of the nineteen climbs are trad, with a handful of bolted lines and one short ice route. Grades cluster between 5.8 and 5.10, with a couple of 5.11s and some easier warm-up options, so it suits a range of parties. Lines run up to about four pitches, which makes it a handy place for first multi-pitch days. Parking is beside the road, so the walk to the base is short. A boulder field sits at the foot of the cliff.

wa_lost_resort.blurb: The biggest wall in Bob's Area, up the Mt Washington trail at Exit 38 near North Bend. It is a steep, all-sport face with nineteen routes, mostly 5.10 to 5.12 and a single 5.13, so it is a place for people already climbing double digits. The wall faces north and gets almost no sun, which makes it a good pick for summer heat, and it dries quickly after wet weather. The hike in is a long one, a couple of miles from the trailhead lot, so it sees fewer people than the crags near the road.

wa_sport_wall.blurb: A section of the Upper Town Wall above the town of Index, holding nineteen routes that are almost all bolted. The climbing is technical, on near-vertical faces, and it is firmly a wall for strong sport climbers: most routes fall around 5.12, with a few 5.11s and a handful at 5.13. There are one or two trad lines mixed in. Reaching it takes the longer upper-wall walk from the lower parking area, roughly half an hour, then a turn left along the base. It is not a spot for beginners.

wa_a_main_wall_west.blurb: The largest section of the Main Wall on Mt Erie, the forested hill above Anacortes on Fidalgo Island. It has about equal numbers of sport and trad routes, nineteen in all, with grades from 5.7 to 5.11 and most in the 5.7 to 5.10 range. The textured diorite offers plenty of holds but few continuous cracks. The wall sits above Snag Buttress, so most parties reach it by climbing a route at the base first. Mt Erie sits in a rain shadow and is often dry, with March through October the best stretch.

wa_great_northern_slab.blurb: A slab at the west end of the Lower Town Wall in Index, just a short walk from the parking lot. It is mostly trad, with a few bolted routes among its nineteen lines. Grades run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk at moderate to 5.10, and most routes take two or three pitches. Many climbers have their first Index day here. It is sunny when the sun is out, so hot afternoons are better spent on the shadier walls nearby, while trees shade the belay spots lower down.
